The `split()` method takes a regular expression as input, which in this case is `(?<=\\G.{k})`. This regular expression matches any position in the input string that is preceded by a lookbehind assertion `\\G`, which matches the position at the beginning of the input or at the end of the previous match. The `k` variable is the input parameter and is inserted into the regular expression using string concatenation.

The resulting string array is then passed to the `allMatch()` method, which returns `true` if all the predicates in the array return `true`, or `false` otherwise.

The `allMatch()` method accepts a predicate which in this case is the `contains()` method with the substring as input. The `contains()` method returns `true` if the input string contains the given substring, or `false` otherwise.

Therefore, the method returns `true` if all the substrings of length `k` in the input string are present in the original string, and `false` otherwise.

The time complexity of this method is O(n \* k), where `n` is the length of the input string `s`. The space complexity is O(n), as an additional string array of length `n` is created to store the split substrings.
